key_insight: Brookfield DV3TLV viscosity readings can be converted into reliable shear-rate and viscosity estimates when geometry-specific empirical correction factors are applied and their validity limits are respected.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to estimate fluid rheology in industrial settings, especially where high-end rheometers are unavailable or too difficult to deploy.
method: Compared Brookfield DV3TLV measurements against a high-precision Anton Paar MCR 302 rheometer.
Tested both Newtonian fluids (water, glycerol) and non-Newtonian guar-based gels.
Derived empirical speed-to-shear-rate coefficients for each measuring geometry and checked Reynolds numbers to confirm laminar flow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cross-validation with the MCR 302 rheometer and shows that Brookfield data can estimate real viscosity with geometry-specific accuracy under the studied operating conditions.
watch_item: The correction factors are geometry- and condition-dependent, so the method should not be transferred blindly outside the tested spindle, speed, and fluid ranges.
paper_title: Quantitative interpretation of Brookfield DV3TLV measurements: shear rate conversion, correction factors, and applicability limits
